NEW DELHI: For decades, Kerala has been the heartbeat of Indian football. Floodlit local tournaments draw packed crowds, school grounds produce gifted footballers, and the sport is woven into the state's cultural identity. Yet translating that passion into a sustainable professional football ecosystem has remained elusive.As the third season of the Super League Kerala (SLK) prepares to kick off on September 25, the league believes it has found a different path. Rather than chasing the glamour of bigger leagues or relying on broadcast windfalls, SLK is attempting to build what its CEO and Director, Mathew Joseph, calls a "360-degree sustainability" model, one where clubs, vendors, grassroots academies and fans all become stakeholders in the game's future.Joseph is candid that Indian football's biggest challenge isn't attracting investors, but ensuring they stay."Our focus from the beginning has been sustainability. It has just not been a sustainability for the league, but a 360-degree sustainability for every stakeholder," he tells TimesofIndia.com in a virtual conversation.The "360-degree sustainability" philosophy influences almost every decision the league makes.SLK has introduced a strict salary cap, fixed player and technical staff budgets, centralised vendors to reduce operational costs, and revenue-sharing mechanisms designed to prevent financial disparity between clubs.Last season, the combined expenditure of the league and its teams approached Rs 90 crore, with the league itself investing around Rs 30 crore while individual clubs spent between Rs eight-10 crore. The player purse has been capped at Rs 1.75 crore (±10%), while technical staff budgets are limited to Rs 25 lakh (±10%). Teams are penalised for both overspending and underspending to maintain competitive balance."The entire model has been worked out in such a way that the teams, apart from the league, the next biggest stakeholder is the teams. In fact, all put together, the teams are more important than us. Because if anyone drops out or if the profitability or the sustainability is affected, they will not stay back. There is a limit to which anyone can bring in money," explained Joseph.The economic model allows the clubs to retain 100% of their own ticketing, sponsorship, merchandise and academy revenues. Only centrally generated league income is pooled, with 40% currently distributed to clubs, while future broadcast rights would see 60% flow directly to teams.Despite its name, Joseph insists Super League Kerala has never positioned itself as a regional league."From day one, I was very clear that we are not just a regional league. I could have gone to a regional channel here and said that we are a regional league, can you broadcast us? We were with Star Sports, HotStar, Sony, Doordarshan, Sports.com, Etisalat in UAE and now we are with Zee5 (Unite8 Sports). This is for the nation. We are building up football in India," said Joseph.Given Kerala's large population that has settled across the world, the league looks to target an audience far beyond its borders.With large Malayali communities spread across the Middle East, Europe and North America, SLK views the diaspora as an important audience. But Joseph believes quality football can also attract supporters from neighbouring southern states.His bigger bet, however, is digital consumption."This year our focus has been on digital first. With Zee5 being our OTT partner, they are ready to take it across the world because most of the Indians who have smart TVs have access to Zee5. So most of the Indians and Keralaites will have access to the league. It should actually help us stream it better," said Joseph.Additionally, the league is looking at exploring vertical mobile broadcasts, multiple camera angles for viewers, and interactive viewing experiences tailored for smartphones, an acknowledgement that many Indian households have a single television but multiple mobile screens.Perhaps the most visible innovation this SLK season will come on the pitch.For the first time in Indian football, every group-stage match will produce a winner. If teams finish level after 90 minutes, the match goes directly to a penalty shootout. A regulation victory earns three points, a shootout win two, a shootout loss one, and a regulation defeat none.Joseph believes eliminating draws will fundamentally change the spectator experience."We will have, definitely, a decision at the end of the match. FIFA has given permissions to such things in Japan, China and a few other countries. So, we are introducing that and this is going to make it more interesting for any spectator or a person who is watching it on television," said Joseph.SLK has also expanded its knockout stage to include home-and-away semi-finals, increasing the season from 33 to 35 matches.Long before launching the league, SLK had already invested in youth football. According to Joseph, the organisation has operated 52 academies, trained over 17,000 children, and built its own talent identification programme (Project Game Changer) in collaboration with the Andrés Iniesta Academy.This year's scouting programme attracted around 3,500 players across six locations in Kerala, with club scouts evaluating prospects for every franchise."Our focus for the last six years since 2020 has been to develop a grassroots (system). We had scouts present year-round at university matches, inter-school, inter-college matches. Last year, out of about 2000-odd children who came, we shortlisted close to about 15, took them into camps, and finally about five of them got selected into various Super League Kerala teams," Joseph said.The league's ambition isn't merely to produce players for the top-tier Kerala Blasters."We are not a feeder system to (Kerala) Blasters. We are a feeder system, or we would love to be a feeder system, for the entire ecosystem of football across the country. It can be another regional league, it can be a national league, it can be an I-League (now IFL) or it can be ISL, anything. As long as people play and get an opportunity elsewhere, we are more than happy," Joseph said, presenting his vision.One success story is Muhammed Sinan, who emerged through Project Game Changer before becoming one of Kannur Warriors' standout performers and earning national recognition. He returns for season three alongside experienced Indian players such as Prasanth K, Abdul Hakku Nediyodath and Pragyan Sundar Gogoi, while overseas recruits include Varo Álvarez, Asier Gomez, Ernesten Lavsamba and Grace Adieu Youmou.SLK continues to mandate experienced overseas footballers and Pro Licence coaches, not simply to improve match quality but to accelerate player development."We try to bring in players who are experienced, who have better footballing knowledge, who have played with many other leagues," said Joseph.Joseph argues that young Indian footballers develop faster when surrounded by professionals who have competed across different football cultures.Season three also features accomplished coaches including Karim Bencherifa (Malappuram FC), Vital Borkelmans (Forca Kochi), Andrey Chernyshov (Kannur Warriors) and Ever Adriano Demaldé (Calicut FC), giving local players access to diverse tactical philosophies.If Indian football is waiting for broadcasters to rescue its finances, Joseph believes it's waiting for the wrong solution. "I don't think linear television is going to pay anymore," he says plainly.Instead, SLK is exploring subscription models, season passes, pay-per-view products and nearly 20 separate revenue streams currently being structured alongside management and accounting firm KPMG. The objective is to create measurable fan commitment rather than speculative club valuations.He also sees infrastructure as the next frontier. The league deliberately postponed expansion from six to eight teams this year because stadiums in prospective cities weren't ready."We thought we could, but we realized that in the five months' time, we will not be able to do justice to that place," he reasoned.Ultimately, Joseph believes clubs must own or control their stadiums if they are to become genuinely valuable sporting institutions.For now, though, season three represents another important step rather than the finished product. Bigger audiences, fuller stadiums, improved technology and stronger grassroots pathways are the immediate targets.As Kerala prepares for another footballing autumn, the league's ambition extends well beyond crowning another champion. It wants to prove that Indian football's next sustainable success story can begin not in the country's biggest cities, but in the state that has loved the game the longest.
Article Summary: The third season of the Super League Kerala (SLK) prepares to kick off on September 25. SLK is attempting to build what its CEO and Director, Mathew Joseph, calls a "360-degree sustainability" model. Joseph says Indian football's biggest challenge isn't attracting investors, but ensuring they stay.

Article Title: 'Ek ball karane do, please' - From boxing rings to 147 first-class wickets: Bishworjit Konthoujam’s unlikely journey began with one request
Article Text:
Bishworjit Konthoujam

The accidental cricketer

One conversation changed everything

Learning the art of fast bowling

Manipur’s wicket machine

Bowling on slopes and in the rain

The meeting with Vaibhav Sooryavanshi

NEW DELHI: When North East Zone pacer Bishworjit Konthoujam came into the attack during the Duleep Trophy quarterfinal against East Zone, all eyes were on the batter facing him - 15-year-old batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.The expectations were clear. Boundaries. Big hits. Perhaps even a few towering sixes.And Sooryavanshi did exactly what many expected from him. After playing out his first two balls, the young batter hit the Manipur pacer for two boundaries in a row. He had taken Konthoujam on.But the 30-year-old had the last laugh.Soon after being hit for the two fours, Konthoujam dismissed Sooryavanshi, ending the young star's stay at the crease. The pacer leapt into the air in celebration before receiving high-fives from his teammates.For many watching, it was just another wicket. For Bishworjit, however, the moment was a reminder of how far he had travelled. Because before he began troubling batters with a cricket ball, he was busy throwing punches in a boxing ring.Before picking up a leather ball, Bishworjit Konthoujam wore boxing gloves. Jab. Cross. Hook.Uppercut.Boxing was his first love. He won medals at school and state-level competitions. He trained hard and dreamed of making a career in the sport.But there was another game he enjoyed - cricket.Like many youngsters in India, Bishworjit loved the game. However, he played only for fun. Whenever he found a group of children playing cricket in his village, he wanted to join them.Walking through the streets of Patsoi Part IV, his residence in Manipur, if he saw youngsters playing cricket, he would often stop and ask: “Ek ball karane do, please” - let me bowl just one ball.He played cricket whenever he had time away from his boxing training.“Cricket was always my second love after boxing. But I never imagined that one day I would leave boxing and become a cricketer,” Bishworjit told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interview.“I give a lot of credit to Ronel sir. Whatever I am today is because of him. He saw something in me and pushed me towards cricket. Leaving boxing wasn't easy at all,” he said.Leishangthem Ronel Singh, secretary of the Manipur Cricket Association, first noticed Bishworjit while he was bowling with a tennis ball during a local game. The young boxer had never received formal cricket coaching, but his bowling caught Ronel's attention.He had pace. He could move the ball. And he had a natural bowling action.Ronel was impressed and suggested that Bishworjit should seriously consider cricket. Bishworjit took his time before making the decision. Then he decided to give the sport a chance. He put his boxing gloves aside and picked up a leather ball.That was the beginning of a journey that would eventually take him from local grounds in Manipur to the Ranji Trophy and Duleep Trophy.“I had never played proper cricket with a leather ball, so it was very difficult in the beginning,” Bishworjit said.“Boxing taught me many things. It taught me how to fight, how to come back and how to get up after falling down. I needed all those things in cricket as well. Leather-ball cricket was completely new to me, but slowly cricket became everything for me.”Switching from tennis-ball cricket to leather-ball cricket was not easy. The grip was different. The release was different. The ball behaved differently.Bishworjit had to learn everything from the beginning. But his years in boxing had made him physically strong and mentally tough. He quickly adapted to the demands of fast bowling.After playing in local tournaments, Bishworjit began making a name for himself in Manipur. He represented the state at the U-23 level before getting the big break he had been waiting for.He made his first-class debut for Manipur against Sikkim in 2018.There was no looking back after that.Bishworjit made an immediate impact in the 2018-19 Ranji Trophy season. He finished as Manipur's highest wicket-taker, picking up 30 wickets in just eight matches. He was also among the top 10 wicket-takers in the country that season.Since then, he has become one of the most successful cricketers from the state.The right-arm medium pacer has played 48 first-class matches, 49 List A games and 46 T20 matches. He has taken 147 wickets in first-class cricket, including three five-wicket hauls. He also has 66 List A and 46 T20 wickets to his name.He was also Manipur's leading wicket-taker in the 2018-19 Vijay Hazare Trophy.In the 2019-20 Vijay Hazare Trophy, he produced a memorable seven-wicket haul, including a hat-trick, against Nagaland.Bishworjit has also taken five-wicket hauls against Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram in the Ranji Trophy.He became the first fast bowler from the North East Zone to take more than 100 first-class wickets and the second player from the region overall to reach the mark. He was also the first player from the North East to take more than 50 wickets in List A cricket.Today, Bishworjit is the leading wicket-taker from the North East Zone across all three formats.His journey also took him beyond India when he became the first cricketer from Manipur to play for an English club, Tynemouth Cricket Club.Bishworjit's journey was far from easy. Before Manipur became a full member of the BCCI and entered India's major domestic tournaments, the state had limited cricket facilities.For a fast bowler, finding a proper place to train was a major challenge.Manipur also receives heavy rainfall for several months every year, making regular outdoor practice difficult.Bishworjit and other young cricketers had to find their own ways to train.“We did not have many facilities before 2018. It rains heavily in Manipur from June to September, so practising was very difficult,” he said.“Sometimes we practised on slopes because we felt running uphill could help us build strength and generate more pace. After the rain, we would put sand on wet areas to make the surface usable and then start bowling again.”The situation, he says, has changed significantly now.The BCCI has helped improve cricket infrastructure in the state, with players now having access to better training facilities.“Things have changed a lot. The BCCI has done a great job for cricket in Manipur and given us much better facilities,” he said.“Life has become much easier for young cricketers now. They have facilities that we did not have when we started.”North East Zone lost the Duleep Trophy quarterfinal, but Bishworjit still wanted to meet Sooryavanshi after the match.The 30-year-old walked towards the East Zone dressing room and met the teenager. They shared a smile and shook hands.Bishworjit had watched Sooryavanshi closely during his rise in the IPL, the Under-19 World Cup and international cricket.“He is a very nice boy and a special talent. I have watched him in the IPL, the Under-19 World Cup and for India. The way he hits the ball is incredible,” Bishworjit said.“But I also told him that red-ball cricket requires patience. You have to give yourself some time at the crease.”Sooryavanshi had shown his attacking style by hitting Bishworjit for two boundaries before the pacer got his wicket.For the Manipur bowler, it was a small example of the difference between white-ball and red-ball cricket.“He had a lot of time to bat. That is the difference between red-ball and white-ball cricket,” Bishworjit said.“In red-ball cricket, patience is very important. You cannot play every ball the way you do in white-ball cricket. We spoke about cricket and exchanged a few thoughts,” he said.
Article Summary: Bishworjit Konthoujam is a fast bowling pacer for North East Zone in the Duleep Trophy. The 30-year-old used to play cricket for fun in his village in Manipur, India. Boxing was his first love and he won medals at school and state level competitions.

Article Title: 'I'm Surprised': Levon Aronian on weakness Praggnanandhaa fixed to win India's historic GCT title | Exclusive
Article Text:
Levon Aronian opens up about R Praggnanandhaa's GCT title

GM Levon Aronian will return to GCL after playing and winning the inaugural edition of the tournament in 2023.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A year ago, American Grandmaster Levon Aronian beat Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa in their third-place match at the Grand Chess Tour (GCT) Finals in São Paulo, Brazil. Playing fast-paced chess, he gradually came to understand one thing. Blitz and rapid, the Armenian great had apprehended, were the young Indian's soft spots.Last Thursday in St Louis, that same soft spot helped Praggnanandhaa script history.He beat Fabiano Caruana 15-13 in the GCT Finals, becoming the first Indian and only the seventh player in the event's 11-year history to lift the title, pocketing $200,000 in the process.He got there by winning both rapid games in the final before holding a four-game blitz section to a 4-4 draw, the exact terrain Aronian once flagged as his weakness."After last year's GCT finals, where I beat him, I thought that blitz and rapid are his weak points, and that should be exploited. And to be honest, I'm surprised. I think he made good progress in those aspects," Aronian, who remains one of the most respected voices in the chess world, told TimesofIndia.com ahead of the new Global Chess League (GCL) season in Bengaluru, where he will represent the Ganges Grandmasters this September.It's a rare thing for one elite player to publicly credit another for closing a gap that was, not long ago, exploited to beat them. "You have to compliment and congratulate somebody who's working hard to fix their weaknesses," the 43-year-old Grandmaster said. "So I'm happy for him because he's a fighter and he's a very likeable person."Aronian isn't the only voice from the sport's old guard taking notice.Earlier, Viswanathan Anand , who returns to the board with Alaskan Knights for this year's GCL, went further still in a separate conversation with this website, calling Praggnanandhaa the best player right now."In Norway Chess, he was not doing well. At some point, there were four rounds left, and he was in the bottom. And then he won four games in a row," Anand explained."He did something similar here, though his performance was much better in Grand Chess Tour and also in the Rapid. He won the Rapid, did well enough in the Blitz to win the tournament. Then he was sort of competing for first place here."He has this capacity, and it's becoming more and more noticeable that he's able to win late games and change everything. And that's a very, very rare skill and useful skill to have."Read also: Amid 'very long meetings' and running chess world, has Viswanathan Anand lost 'hunger' to win? | Exclusive "I think at the moment, I would say he's the number one player in the world," Anand opined, pointing to the same capacity for turnarounds that Aronian's comments now echo from the losing end of one."Well, Magnus (Carlsen) doesn't compete in the same events, but nonetheless, you know, if you take classical included, and I know Pragg, in the tournaments which happened in August and all, he performed incredibly well. If you go back to Norway Chess and then see the development from there, I think it's just fantastic."
Article Summary: GM Levon Aronian will return to GCL after playing and winning the inaugural edition of the tournament in 2023. Praggnanandhaa became the first Indian and only the seventh player in the event's 11-year history to lift the title, pocketing $200,000 in the process.

Article Text:
Aryna Sabalenka

World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka cut short a reporter's question during her post-match press conference after being asked whether the events and brand appearances before the US Open had involved "parties and fun. "The exchange came after the defending champion Sabalenka's 6-1, 6-1 win over Polina Iatcenko in the second round on Wednesday. It was the second straight press conference in which she was asked about her activities before the tournament.The defending champion rejected the suggestion that her off-court appearances had affected her preparation."You guys are, like, a joke. Parties, fun... like, why would you even say that? Why would you even think about that? What kind of question is that?" Sabalenka said."Just because I posted, like, some activities with brands, and you think that I've been partying, not training?" she added before ending the exchange.After the discussion moved back to tennis, Sabalenka said she was happy with her performance and the way she has approached matches."I've been working really hard, but I feel like I'm kind of moving away from trying to be perfect on court," Sabalenka said. "I know that you cannot be perfect, and I'm just trying to work with what I have right now."The Belarusian is chasing a third straight US Open title while also looking to avoid finishing the year without a Grand Slam title. Her last title came at the Miami Open in March.Sabalenka admitted she went through a difficult period during the middle of the season but believes she has recovered both mentally and physically."I think I struggled a little bit in the middle of the season. Once again, I'm not going to defend myself or explain why, what happened, but I'm happy with my level," the 28-year-old said."I can definitely say that mentally I'm way stronger than I was in the middle of the season, and physically I also feel stronger. I feel like I'm on my level of play, and I just want to bring the right focus on the match every time."
Article Summary: Aryna Sabalenka cut short a reporter's question during her post-match press conference. She was asked whether the events and brand appearances before the US Open had involved "parties and fun" The exchange came after the defending champion beat Polina Iatcenko in the second round on Wednesday.

Article Title: David White steps down as ILT20 CEO after three-year stint
Article Text:
David White joined the ILT20 as CEO in September 2023 and oversaw the league during its first three seasons from 2023 to 2025.

NEW DELHI: The International League T20 (ILT20) on Thursday has announced that Chief Executive Officer David White will leave his position after requesting not to extend his contract and deciding to return to his home country, New Zealand.White joined the ILT20 as CEO in September 2023 and oversaw the league during its first three seasons from 2023 to 2025.ILT20 chairman Khalid Al Zarooni thanked White for his contribution to the league's growth during his tenure."The ILT20 team acknowledges the hard work and commitment of David White as the league's CEO during his three-year stay and thanks him for his services," Al Zarooni said."Under White, the league made great progress and succeeded in establishing itself as one of the major tournaments in the world. White played a leading role in the league's growth during his tenure. We wish him the very best in his future endeavours."White said he had decided to return to New Zealand after three successful years with the league."I have decided to return to my home country, New Zealand, after three hugely successful years with the International League T20. I am grateful to the ILT20 for accepting my request," White said."I thoroughly enjoyed my stint at the league, which in recent years has grown into one of the top T20 tournaments in the world."I want to take this opportunity to thank the ILT20 management, the Emirates Cricket Board, my colleagues, tournament franchises and partners for their tremendous work and support. I wish the ILT20 the very best in the years ahead."
Article Summary: David White joined the ILT20 as CEO in September 2023 and oversaw the league during its first three seasons from 2023 to 2025. White said he had decided to return to New Zealand after three successful years with the league.ILT20 chairman Khalid Al Zarooni thanked White for his contribution to the league's growth during his tenure.

Article Title: 'All issues sorted': Five years after Krunal Pandya row, Deepak Hooda set to play for Baroda
Article Text:
Deepak Hooda, Krunal Pandya

Hard-hitting batter Deepak Hooda is set to return to his home team Baroda in domestic cricket five years after moving to Rajasthan "Yes, Deepak is coming back to Baroda. He and Krunal (Pandya) have spoken to each other. Everything is sorted between them," Baroda Cricket Association (BCA) CEO Snehal Parikh confirmed to TOI on Thursday.The batting allrounder had joined Rajasthan as a professional for the 2021-22 domestic season after severing ties with Baroda. Hooda had moved to Rajasthan after being banned for the 2020-21 season in January by the BCA for "indiscipline."Hooda moved out of the team hotel on the eve of the Baroda's first match in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy in January 2021, alleging that Baroda captain Krunal Pandya 's "bad behaviour", abusive language and "bullying" had made him "depressed, demoralised and under pressure" and forced him to walk out.However, Parikh said that "all issues between BCA and Hooda had been sorted now."In 67 first-class matches, the 31-year-old Hooda has scored 4267 runs at 45.39, with 14 centuries and 18 half-centuries, and a highest score of 293 not out. He has also taken 29 wickets@41.44, with a best haul of five for 31.In 109 list A matches, he has scored 3340 runs at 38.83, with six centuries and 17 half-centuries, and a highest score of 104, besides taking 42 wickets at 29.92, with a best haul of five for 55.In 230 T20s, Hooda has stroked 3972 runs@24.67, with two centuries, and a highest score of 108.Hooda has played 10 ODIs (153 runs at 25.50 & three wickets at 39.66) and 21 T20Is (368 runs at 30.66, six wickets at 12.66), though he last played for India in a T20I against New Zealand on February 1 2023.Meanwhile, 'keeper-batter Jitesh Sharma will continue to represent Baroda as a guest player, but only in white-ball formats, Parikh informed.
Article Summary: Deepak Hooda set to return to home team Baroda in domestic cricket. Batsman had joined Rajasthan as a professional for 2021-22 domestic season after severing ties with Baroda. Jitesh Sharma will continue to represent Baroda as guest player, but only in white-ball formats.

Article Title: 'It’s impossible': Carlos Alcaraz reveals he will take 'long breaks' from tennis
Article Text:
Carlos Alcaraz, of Spain, returns the ball to Jaime Faria, of Portugal, during the second round of the U.S. Open tennis championships, Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Sydney Schaefer)

Alcaraz concerned about player workload

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Carlos Alcaraz says he plans to take regular breaks from tennis in the future, even if that means skipping some tournaments. The Spaniard believes the packed ATP calendar is becoming too demanding and could leave players exhausted or injured.The defending US Open champion made the comments after fighting back from a first-set loss to beat Portugal’s Jaime Faria 4-6, 6-0, 6-3, 6-2 and reach the third round.Alcaraz recently returned after missing four months because of a wrist injury. While he did not want that long break, he now feels shorter, planned breaks could help him stay fresh.“I took more than I wanted, to be honest, but seeing how tight is the calendar, obviously I don’t want to have this break because an injury. But in the future, I’m going to take some breaks, some long breaks. Maybe not four months, but one month, two months, missing some tournaments, because it’s impossible to play them all,” Alcaraz said.The 22-year-old feels players are being pushed to compete in too many major events, leaving little time to recover.“I think they adding more important tournaments. In a way they making us to play,” Alcaraz said. “You can decide your calendar, but there are some Masters 1000s, some Grand Slams, and we’ve been out playing 40 weeks if we got to play every mandatory tournament that the ATP required us to play,” he added.“So it’s impossible, and we are seeing a lot of players getting injured, a lot of players getting tired. If they don’t do anything about it, we are going to see even more in the future,” he warned.On court, Alcaraz recovered impressively after dropping the opening set. He won eight games in a row and broke Faria’s serve five times consecutively to take control.The Spaniard hit 43 winners and converted seven of 12 break points to complete the comeback. The victory extended his Grand Slam winning streak to 16 matches and improved his US Open record to 26-3.Alcaraz, a two-time US Open champion, is now 9-0 at the majors in 2026. He next faces China’s Wu Yibing.
Article Summary: Carlos Alcaraz says he plans to take regular breaks from tennis in the future, even if that means skipping some tournaments. The Spaniard believes the packed ATP calendar is becoming too demanding and could leave players exhausted or injured. The defending US Open champion made the comments after fighting back from a first-set loss to beat Portugal’s Jaime Faria 4-6, 6-0,. 6-3, 6 -2 and reach the third round.

Carlos Alcaraz made a winning return to Grand Slam tennis at the US Open on Monday, and the biggest positive was that his injured right wrist felt completely fine.The 23-year-old Spaniard beat Roman Safiullin 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 despite missing the French Open and Wimbledon since April.“I don’t know how it looked from outside, but from inside, my feeling was that I was hitting normal,” Alcaraz said. “I was playing pretty normal, playing my style, and yeah, the arm, the wrist, everything felt great.”Alcaraz admitted he was more nervous than usual because he had not played a Grand Slam match for several months. Still, he said his main aim was to enjoy the tournament and see how his body responds.“I had more nerves than usual, but just happy, because, for me, my goal here is to compete, to enjoy, and let’s see how my body’s going to react after the matches, after the competition again,” Alcaraz said.“I don’t know how far I’m going to go in the tournament. I didn’t know if I was going to lose this one, if I’m going to make the second round, final. I don’t know how far I’m going to go. But what I just really want to do is enjoy every time that I’m going to walk into the court feeling the energy from the people, feel the competition.”His chances of defending the title have received a boost after Novak Djokovic suffered a shock first-round defeat, while top-ranked Jannik Sinner is sidelined with a knee injury.Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka also began strongly, beating Camila Osorio 6-4, 6-4. She is aiming to become the first player since Serena Williams to win three straight US Open titles.“I feel like this is one of my favorite stadiums,” Sabalenka told the crowd afterward. “I really experienced the best emotions here in this stadium.”Meanwhile, Stefanos Tsitsipas eliminated 10th seed Arthur Fils and was asked whether he could rediscover his best form.“Why not?” Tsitsipas said.
Article Summary: Carlos Alcaraz makes winning return to Grand Slam tennis at US Open. Spaniard beat Roman Safiullin despite missing French Open and Wimbledon. Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka also began strongly. Stefanos Tsitsipas eliminated 10th seed Arthur Fils.

Article Title: Rohit Rajpal throws hat into ring for AITA president’s post
Article Text:
DLTA president Rohit Rajpal announces candidature for All India Tennis Association presidency

New Delhi:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Rohit Rajpal has thrown his hat into the ring for the All India Tennis Association (AITA) president’s post, setting up a potentially keen contest ahead of elections likely to be held in late Oct or early Nov this year.The AITA is currently functioning under the interim supervision of court-appointed administrator, retired Justice Gita Mittal. The administrator has opened the process for Sportsperson of Outstanding Merit (SOM) candidates seeking to contest the elections for AITA office-bearer posts.Rajpal, 55, will contest through the general body and file his nomination through his state association. He is currently president of the Delhi Lawn Tennis Association (DLTA), an Executive Committee member of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), an AITA office-bearer and the non-playing captain of the Indian Davis Cup team.“It is after a lot of introspection and interactions with well-wishers in the tennis fraternity and other friends that I have decided to contest the forthcoming elections of the prestigious All India Tennis Association as President,” Rajpal said in a statement.“Tennis is not just a sport for me; it has been my life since the time I was a young boy who wished to make it big. At 55, when many summers have passed, my heart still beats for Indian tennis.It is my dream and vision for India that a sport which has produced so many champions at home should grow further by leaps and bounds,” he added.Rajpal, a former Asian Junior champion and Asian Games medallist whose playing career was cut short by a serious back injury, said his experience in tennis administration and the Davis Cup had strengthened his resolve to seek the top post.“Having been involved in tennis matters at large for almost a decade in AITA and DLTA has been a learning and enriching hands-on experience,” he said. “As the non-playing Davis Cup captain of Team India in several Davis Cup engagements, it was enormously satisfying to be with and motivate our immensely talented players to give their best and bring glory to the nation by advancing to the second-round qualifiers.”India will face South Korea in Seoul on September 18-19 for a place in the final eight of the Davis Cup. Rajpal, however, will have to relinquish the Davis Cup captaincy if he is elected AITA president.“This journey has given me the confidence to now step forward and announce my candidature as President of All India Tennis Association as a step forward in my desire to contribute to the growth and development of tennis in India,” Rajpal said.“With your support, I plan to adopt player-centric approach and policies, good governance and transparency above all. I plan to share my vision document in due course,” he added.Chintan Parikh of the Gujarat association is also expected to contest the president’s post. It is learnt that Indian tennis legend and Bengal Tennis Association president Leander Paes could also enter the fray. Paes, who took charge of the Bengal association in Nov 2025, would likely come through the SOM route and file his nomination.
Article Summary: Rohit Rajpal has thrown his hat into the ring for the All India Tennis Association (AITA) president’s post. Rajpal, 55, will contest through the general body and file his nomination through his state association. Bengal Tennis Association president Leander Paes could also enter the fray.

Article Title: Siddhesh Lad to replace Shardul Thakur as Mumbai captain for 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season
Article Text:
Siddhesh Lad and Shardul Thakur (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Mumbai: Mumbai will have a new captain for the second successive Ranji Trophy season, with seasoned batter Siddhesh Lad set to take charge of the 42-time champions in the 2026-27 campaign. Lad will replace allrounder Shardul Thakur , who led Mumbai across formats during the previous domestic season.Confirming the development, Mumbai senior selection committee chairman Rajesh Pawar said the decision was taken keeping both leadership continuity and workload management in mind.“Yes, we’ve decided to appoint Siddhesh as our captain for the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season. He did well last season and is experienced. Shardul is our match-winner. There is already too much workload on him as he’s expected to bowl a lot of overs, take wickets and contribute with the bat as well. We don’t want to burden him with the responsibility of captaincy. Plus, we’ll have to manage his workload. There are 10 games in the Ranji Trophy and he may have to rest for the odd match,” Pawar told TOI on Monday.Pawar said both players had been consulted before the move was finalised.“We’ve spoken to both Siddhesh and Shardul about it, and both are positive about it. Since the season starts with four Ranji Trophy matches in October, we wanted clarity on the captaincy well in advance,” he added.The appointment rewards a stellar domestic season from Lad, who was Mumbai’s standout performer with the bat in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy. The 34-year-old amassed 774 runs in eight matches at an impressive average of 77.40, striking five centuries to finish as the team’s leading run-scorer.Over the course of an accomplished first-class career, Lad has compiled 5,623 runs in 82 matches at 44.27, including 15 hundreds and 30 fifties. Mumbai begin their Ranji Trophy season against Chandigarh at Wankhede Stadium from Oct 11-14. They are placed in Elite Group D alongside Chandigarh, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Railways, Tamil Nadu and Uttarakhand. Mumbai last lifted the Ranji Trophy in 2023-2024 under Ajinkya Rahane.
Article Summary: Siddhesh Lad will captain Mumbai in the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season. The 34-year-old replaces Shardul Thakur, who led Mumbai across formats last season. Mumbai begin their campaign against Chandigarh at Wankhede Stadium from Oct 11-14.

Article Title: ‘Nothing went according to my plans’: K Humpy opens up ahead of Olympiad title defence
Article Text:
K Humpy

TOI

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

K Humpy, India’s top-ranked woman chess player, was unwilling to state her preferred board number for Team India at the Olympiad. Nor did she say that she would play according to the wishes of the team or captain. But she dropped enough hints.“I have played a few Olympiads and have always played on board one. For many years, we have been following the rating procedure for maintaining the board order. I don’t know how they are going to look at it this year,” Humpy toldfrom Vijayawada on Monday. Top seeds India are set to defend their gold medal in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, starting Sept 16.Humpy finished eighth with 3.5 points in the nine-round classical Cairns Cup in St Louis, USA. But her Norway Chess campaign in May-June, where she finished sixth and last, was particularly disappointing. “It’s not so comfortable to enter into the Olympiad in such a scenario,” said Humpy. “I'm just waiting to get back in good shape. I was a bit rusty but it happens to every player. You’ll be in that bad phase and then you’ll come out of it.On her poor run in Norway, Humpy said, “I played the tournament after a very long gap.Nothing went according to my plans. This year was disturbing. I was also a bit upset with the off-the-board things and probably that also reflected in the way I played.”Humpy withdrew from the Candidates tournament in Cyprus after FIDE turned down her request to shift the eight-player women’s world championship qualifier to a safer venue, citing security concerns arising from the war in West Asia.“I think I’m fine now,” she said. “Probably, it did disturb me for a few months. Like, it’s not easy for a player who has been professional and working towards it and then taking all the negativity. So it did affect me. I spent many sleepless nights as well. But for the last month or so, I have been in better shape.”
Article Summary: K Humpy, India’s top-ranked woman chess player, was unwilling to state her preferred board number for Team India at the Olympiad. Top seeds India are set to defend their gold medal in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, starting Sept 16.

Article Title: ‘Pakistan cricket has hit a panic button’: Ramiz Raja slams PCB over unprecedented England tour overhaul
Article Text:
Pakistan cricket team (ANI Photo)

Ramiz questions unprecedented overhaul

Changes come amid Lord’s controversy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Pakistan batter and PCB chairman Ramiz Raja has criticised the current board for what he described as a panic-driven response to the team’s disastrous Test tour of England.The PCB made sweeping changes after Pakistan lost the first two Tests of the three-match series, sending seven players home before the final match in Birmingham. Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha are among those dropped from the tour, while seven replacements have been brought into the squad.The changes have also extended to the coaching staff. Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant coach Umar Gul have been released from their positions, with white-ball coach Mike Hesson set to take charge for the third Test.Ramiz believes the scale and timing of the overhaul could further damage the confidence of the Pakistan players rather than solve the team’s problems.“I'm trying to convince myself this is all OK, but it is not. It just shows Pakistan cricket has hit a panic button. It's not good for the game, it's not good for the confidence of the players who have come in, or for the players who are left, because it makes you a selfish team,” Ramiz, BBC Radio 5 Live.“What is the guarantee they will get the results? Some of these guys have not played Test cricket. I've got no idea why this was done,” he added.Pakistan’s performances in England have been poor from the outset.They suffered an innings defeat in the opening Test at Headingley before England won the Lord’s Test by 194 runs. Across their four innings in the series, Pakistan have failed to reach 200 on every occasion.However, Ramiz questioned whether replacing such a large number of players midway through a tour could suddenly change the team’s fortunes.“I'm really not happy with the situation. How many times have we seen this happen in world cricket? Never, ever. This is more like football, midway through the season, firing a manager. If you ask me how things can be fixed, I've got no idea,” said Ramiz.The former PCB chairman also pointed to the uncertainty created for both the players being sent home and those suddenly brought into the squad.With the third Test fast approaching, several newcomers will be expected to adapt quickly to Test cricket and the conditions in England.The PCB’s drastic decisions have come during an already turbulent tour.The Lord’s Test was played against the backdrop of an off-field dispute involving the sons of former Pakistan captain and prime minister Imran Khan.Sky Sports broadcast an interview with Suleiman and Kasim Khan during the lunch interval on the opening day. The programme focused on their father’s circumstances and prompted reports that the PCB had considered withdrawing Pakistan from the remainder of the Test and potentially the tour.Pakistan ultimately continued playing, while captain Babar Azam and head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed said they were unaware of any plan to boycott the match.The timing of the latest changes has also attracted attention because the Pakistan squad is scheduled to meet King Charles at Clarence House during its stay in the UK.Pakistan will now attempt to salvage something from the tour when they face England in the third and final Test in Birmingham.
Article Summary: Ramiz questions unprecedented overhaul of Pakistan's cricket team. Seven players have been sent home and seven replacements brought in. Head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant coach Umar Gul have been released from their positions, with white-ball coach Mike Hesson set to take charge for the third Test.

Article Title: Mahela Jayawardene likely to continue as Mumbai Indians coach; status quo on trade chatter
Article Text:
Mahela Jayawardene (left) and Hardik Pandya

Don't be surprised if he [Hardik Pandya] is not traded at all. Discussions have also happened with the player along these lines. For a trade to happen, multiple things need to fall into place. So it's not that straightforward. Sources

Hardik Pandya

NEW DELHI: Former Sri Lanka captain Mahela Jayawardene is likely to continue as Mumbai Indians (MI) head coach for the 2027 edition of the Indian Premier League (IPL), with the franchise reluctant to make sweeping changes. It is learnt that Jayawardene joined the five-time champions on a "two + one" contract in 2024 and could well be given another year, considering it will be the last year of the ongoing cycle. A formal announcement is expected next month, provided there is no late change of heart.Under Jayawardene, Mumbai Indians reached the playoffs in 2025 but finished ninth the following year. 2026 was a disappointing season for the IPL giants, as they won only four games in a campaign marred by injuries, availability concerns and unrest in the dressing room.Since the disappointing last season, there has been a lot of chatter around their captain Hardik Pandya's potential trade. While multiple franchises have expressed interest, there has yet to be any substantial movement on that front.TimesofIndia.com has also learnt that some dialogue has taken place with the Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR), but the lack of a tradeable asset has not excited MI at the moment. Cameron Green's name was on the table, but the MI think tank is wary of the Australian's workload next year, which includes Australia's packed Test calendar.As far as the Chennai Super Kings (CSK) are concerned, some action is expected once they finalise their new head coach.How will MI tackle the Pandya situation? They are keen on retaining him as a player for the upcoming season as they plan to head in a new direction under a new captain. The management has already explored this idea, and it is learnt that former India and MI captain Rohit Sharma is actively involved in discussions about the captaincy and the team's direction. Returning Rohit to the captaincy was also an option, but a new face is likely as the 39-year-old is not keen to wear the armband again. Tilak Varma and Jasprit Bumrah are two potential options, with the scales tilting in the former's favour."Don't be surprised if he is not traded at all. Discussions have also happened with the player along these lines. For a trade to happen, multiple things need to fall into place. So it's not that straightforward," says a source tracking developments.It will be interesting to see how the dynamics unfold if Pandya is not traded at all and how the franchise addresses the dressing room unrest. A change in captaincy is something they expect will restore normalcy, but navigating the turbulence will require significant effort. Another matter that will need attention is that of recently sacked India T20I captain Suryakumar Yadav . Apart from Pandya, there was chatter around the T20 specialist, but the franchise seems in no mood to let go of their experienced campaigner."Yes, he didn't have a good season last year, but what about the ones before that? MI will not discard a player based on one season, and that's not how they operate. They take pride in the 'One Family' tag and swear by it," adds the source.As things stand, continuity has been the bottom line. While a reset cannot be ruled out from the next cycle, there is no desperation for the 2027 edition. A captaincy change is inevitable, but it may not be a surprise if the status quo continues on other matters.
Article Summary: Mahela Jayawardene is likely to continue as Mumbai Indians head coach for the 2027 edition of the Indian Premier League (IPL) The franchise are reluctant to make sweeping changes. A formal announcement is expected next month, provided there is no late change of heart. There has been a lot of chatter around Hardik Pandya's potential trade.

Article Title: 'Good for nothing': Danish Kaneria lambasts Pakistan cricket, calls it 'a shame after 70 years'
Article Text:
Players greet each other at the end of the play on day four of the second cricket test match between England and Pakistan in London, Sunday, Aug. 30, 2026. (AP Photo/Dave Shopland)

Kaneria questions Pakistan’s team and bowling attack

Call for major changes in domestic cricket

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Pakistan spinner Danish Kaneria has strongly criticised the country’s cricket system after Pakistan suffered a 0-2 Test series defeat against England. He questioned the team’s selection, coaching, domestic cricket structure and the lack of accountability within the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB).Pakistan’s 194-run loss at Lord’s gave England an unassailable lead in the series. In response, Pakistan released seven players from the squad and removed head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul. But Kaneria believes changing personnel will not solve the deeper problems.Kaneria said Pakistan’s cricket has lost its competitiveness and the fighting spirit that was once associated with the team. He also criticised the repeated changes in leadership and selection.“It's a shame that after 70 years, Pakistan has gone through such a disaster. There is no logic, selection committee, or play. They are just good for nothing. You see, such a bad performance. If a person loses, he tries and fights before losing. The fight has to be visible. Here, there’s no fight. No one knows anything,” he told news agency IANS.He also questioned why coaches and selectors are appointed for short periods before being removed, saying the system needs stability and people who are willing to take responsibility for both wins and losses.Kaneria was particularly unhappy with Pakistan’s bowling options. He pointed out that experienced players such as Mohammad Abbas, who took nine wickets at Lord’s, and spinner Noman Ali have been overlooked despite performing well.“And the bowling attack is pathetic. Who is Muhammad Shahzad? Where did he come from? He doesn’t have any line or length. No swing, no reverse swing. Nothing.”He also criticised Pakistan’s batting approach in English conditions, particularly the dismissals of Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan.“Like a player of the calibre of Babar Azam is getting out like this. This is pathetic. And then you are keeping Rizwan for so long. I don't know what he is doing. Why is he even there?”Kaneria believes the problems begin well before players reach the national team. He blamed the weakening of domestic cricket and the closure of departmental cricket for reducing the quality of Pakistan’s talent pool.“I like how the BCCI have put in their contracts that first class cricket is important. At least you play 5 to 6 games. None of our boys play domestic. And this downfall of Pakistan cricket started when the structure of domestic cricket changed.”He argued that selectors need to regularly watch domestic matches instead of relying heavily on performances in the Pakistan Super League.“The reason is that the talent pool has been eliminated. There is no doubt there’s talent pool in Pakistan but this selection happens mostly based on PSL.”Kaneria called for a strong selection committee, an experienced coach and a settled group of players who are given enough time to develop.“There are only a few players around whom Pakistan cricket revolves. There is no improvement. Need a strong coach and a strong selection committee.”Above all, he wants Pakistan to regain its competitive spirit.“We also used to lose. But fight and lose. At least fight. Fight, try at least! But there is no effort.”
Article Summary: Former Pakistan spinner Danish Kaneria has strongly criticised the country’s cricket system after Pakistan suffered a 0-2 Test series defeat against England. He questioned the team’S selection, coaching, domestic cricket structure and the lack of accountability within the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB)

Article Title: Big Blow for South Africa! Kagiso Rabada likely to miss Australia Test series with Hamstring Injury

Kagiso Rabada likely to miss Australia Tests (Image: Agency)

Donald confirms Rabada absence

Proteas face pace-bowling concerns

South Africa are likely to suffer a major blow ahead of their three-match Test series against Australia, with premier fast bowler Kagiso Rabada ruled out after sustaining a severe Grade 3 tear in his right hamstring.The injury, picked up during Rabada’s winter conditioning programme, is expected to keep him out for up to 10 weeks, ruling him out of the high-profile series that begins in Durban on October 9.Former South Africa fast bowler and current Lions bowling coach Allan Donald confirmed that Rabada will miss the entire series, ending hopes of having him available for the domestic season.“He’s going to be out for all the Aussie Tests as well,” Donald was quoted as saying by South African media outlet News24 on Sunday.South Africa are scheduled to face Australia in three Tests, with the second match in Gqeberha from October 18 and the final Test in Cape Town from October 27. The series will be preceded by a three-match ODI series beginning in Durban on September 24.Rabada’s absence leaves a significant void in the South African bowling attack. Gerald Coetzee Corbin Bosch and youngster Kwena Maphaka are likely to shoulder greater responsibility in his absence. South Africa are also monitoring the fitness of Nandre Burger, who is recovering from a stress fracture in his back.However, there is still a chance that the left-arm pacer could recover in time to feature in the Test series.Meanwhile, Rabada has taken 340 wickets in 73 Tests and played a key role in South Africa’s victory over Australia in the 2025 World Test Championship final at Lord’s, where he finished with match figures of 9-110. He also boasts an impressive record against Australia, having claimed 58 wickets in 11 Tests at an average of 21.39.

Article Title: Duleep Trophy: Tilak Varma helps South seal final berth
Article Text:
Tilak Varma

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: It was a fitting finish to a match in which Tilak Varma was at the crease every day. The South Zone captain walked out on all four days of the Duleep Trophy semifinal against North Zone and walked back on Wednesday having hit the winning four, sealing a seven-wicket victory and a place in the final against East Zone.Tilak, who had earlier rescued South with a gritty unbeaten century in the first innings, produced another composed half-century on the final day to complete a memorable all-round captaincy effort.Chasing 181, South got off to a steady start as openers Ricky Bhui (42) and N Jagadeesan (43) put on 64. Bhui entertained with a series of fluent strokes before a ramp shot off Gurnoor Brar, caught by Anshul Kamboj at third man, brought his innings to an end.Shaik Rasheed fell in the next over, but there was no further alarm for the South as Tilak stood firm.The left-hander looked assured, playing close to his body against Brar and showing fluency against both pace and spin. His drives were crisp, while the occasional reverse and paddle sweep showed he was willing to improvise without appearing out of control.At the other end, R Smaran (32 n.o) settled in comfortably. He rotated the strike, found the boundary four times and cleared it once before Tilak provided the finishing touch.Earlier, Kerala pacer MD Nidheesh (5/56) wrapped up North Zone’s second innings in the morning, bowling them out for 297 and completing his 10th five-wicket haul in first-class cricket.Nidheesh was relentless with his line and length and disturbed the stumps of Anshul Kamboj, Brar and Arshdeep Singh to finish with five wickets. North added 41 runs to their overnight total.Tilak later said after the match that Karun Nair’s omission from the playing XI was dictated by match-ups rather than form. Karun had scored 699 runs in the last Ranji Trophy season.
Article Summary: South Zone beat North Zone by seven wickets in Duleep Trophy semifinal. Tilak Varma hit the winning four on the final day of the match. Kerala pacer MD Nidheesh took five wickets for the hosts.

Article Title: India set to host ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027
Article Text:
Inaugural ICC Women's Champions Trophy to be held in India from February 14 to 28

MUMBAI: India’s growing grip on global white-ball cricket strengthened further on Wednesday after ICC awarded hosting rights for the inaugural Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 to the country, further underlining the sport’s commercial centre of gravity.Mumbai’s iconic Brabourne Stadium and Vadodara’s Kotambi Stadium will host the six-team tournament in the T20 format from Feb 14-28, 2027 after ICC stripped Sri Lanka of the event because of govt interference in cricket administration.For Mumbai, the decision adds another chapter to the city’s rich history of hosting marquee ICC events. Brabourne Stadium staged the final of the 2013 ICC Women’s ODI World Cup between Australia and West Indies, while the city’s Wankhede Stadium hosted the unforgettable 2011 Men’s ODI World Cup final between India and Sri Lanka, where MS Dhoni’s India lifted the trophy before a packed house. Across the harbour, Navi Mumbai’s DY Patil Stadium hosted the final of the 2025 Women’s ODI World Cup between India and South Africa, further cementing the Mumbai Metropolitan Region’s status as a favoured destination for global cricket showcases.The city had also been a venue for the 2006 ICC Champions Trophy, whose final was played at Brabourne between Australia and West Indies.The latest allotment continues India’s dominance as host of the game’s biggest white-ball events. The country successfully staged the Men’s ODI World Cup in 2023 and the Women’s ODI World Cup in 2025, and is also scheduled to host the 2029 Men’s Champions Trophy.
Article Summary: Inaugural ICC Women's Champions Trophy to be held in India from February 14 to 28, 2027. Mumbai’s iconic Brabourne Stadium and Vadodara's Kotambi Stadium will host the tournament in the T20 format. ICC stripped Sri Lanka of the event because of govt interference in cricket administration.

Pakistan Test team captain Babar Azam met UK's King Charles III in London on Wednesday and presented him with a cricket bat signed by the entire Pakistan team, even as Pakistan's tour of England continues to be overshadowed by defeats and drastic changes in the squad.Babar, along with the Pakistan squad and Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman Mohsin Naqvi, visited Clarence House on September 2. After missing the first Test because of a finger injury, he returned at Lord's but scored only 8 and 6 as Pakistan were bowled out for 110 in the first innings and 194 while chasing a target of 389.The Lord's Test extended Babar's difficult run in the longest format. Article Title: ‘We are not sending legends as replacements’: Former Pakistan batter Mohammad Yousuf lambasts PCB amid ongoing chaos

Pakistan face England changes

Former Pakistan batter Mohammad Yousuf has questioned the major changes made to the Test squad and coaching staff during the ongoing England tour, saying the decisions appear to be linked to the wider instability that has affected Pakistan cricket for years.Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), led by Mohsin Naqvi, made sweeping changes after the team went 2-0 down in the three-Test series. Seven players and two coaching staff members were sent home ahead of the third Test.Yousuf suggested the changes were not based solely on performances and said Pakistan cricket has repeatedly been caught up in internal disagreements and controversies.“The recent decision by the authorities to recall players and coaching staff from the ongoing tour does not appear to be only performance related,” Yousuf wrote on X.“After all, we are not sending legends like Zaheer Abbas, Javed Miandad, Inzamam-ul-Haq, or Saeed Anwar as replacements. Instead, this move reflects the familiar cycle of internal chaos, differences of opinion, and controversies that have long haunted Pakistan cricket,” he added.The former batter, who played 90 Tests and scored more than 7,500 runs for Pakistan, said the problems have continued since the team’s 1992 World Cup triumph.“Since the glory of the 1992 World Cup, such turbulence has resurfaced time and again, eroding stability and distracting from the game itself,” he said.Yousuf’s comments came after Pakistan released Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman, Aamir Jamal, Muhammad Awais Zafar and Khurram Shahzad from the Test squad.Pakistan lost the second Test by 194 runs at Lord’s after suffering an innings-and-103-run defeat in the series opener at Headingley.The PCB also removed red-ball head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and bowling coach Umar Gul, with white-ball head coach Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke taking charge for the remainder of the tour.Yousuf warned that repeated off-field turmoil could hurt the team’s progress and weaken supporters’ confidence.“We have endured such turmoil in different forms many times before, each episode leaving scars on the team’s progress and the fans’ faith,” he wrote.“The lesson is clear! Only strong performances and consistent positive results can silence the noise. Pakistan cricket must focus on the field, not the boardroom, if it is to restore credibility and inspire confidence among fans. Success remains the most effective antidote,” Yousuf concluded.
Article Summary: Mohammad Yousuf questions Pakistan Cricket Board's changes to the Test squad. Seven players and two coaching staff members were sent home ahead of the third Test. Article Title: 11 coaches reset in last five years and still searching for answers: Inside Pakistan cricket’s never-ending coaching carousel
Article Text:
Pakistan’s Coaching Carousel (Agency Images)

From Misbah to Saqlain: The first reset

2023-24: Another major reshuffle

2025: Hesson arrives, Azhar takes red-ball duties

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

2026: Sarfaraz gets the Test job - then loses it mid-series

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe that a split-coaching model (separate coaches for red and white-ball formats) is effective? Yes, it brings specialized focus No, it complicates team dynamics It depends on the coaches' compatibility 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan cricket has developed a familiar pattern over the past five years: a disappointing series or tournament is followed by a management reshuffle, and another coaching regime begins before the previous one has had enough time to establish itself. The latest upheaval came in August 2026, when the Pakistan Cricket Board removed Test head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed after the team lost the first two Tests of the series against England. White-ball head coach Mike Hesson was handed charge of the Test side as Pakistan made sweeping changes ahead of the third Test. Seven players were also sent home.The episode has once again put the spotlight on Pakistan's long-running problem with coaching stability. Since Misbah-ul-Haq stepped down in September 2021, the national team has gone through a succession of permanent, interim and split-format coaching arrangements.Rather than a straightforward line of succession, Pakistan's coaching history in this period resembles a revolving door.Misbah-ul-Haq was appointed head coach and chief selector in 2019, beginning a period in which Pakistan operated under an all-format coaching structure.He and bowling coach Waqar Younis stepped down in September 2021, despite having a year remaining on their contracts.The PCB immediately turned to Saqlain Mushtaq and Abdul Razzaq as interim coaches for the upcoming New Zealand series.Saqlain subsequently became the permanent head coach, overseeing Pakistan across formats until the end of 2022-23. His tenure was followed by another transition in 2023, when the PCB experimented with a new structure involving Grant Bradburn as head coach and Mickey Arthur as team director.Bradburn was formally appointed head coach in May 2023 on a two-year contract after working with the team during the New Zealand series. By the 2023 World Cup, the structure featured Arthur as director, Bradburn as head coach and a wider support staff.Following the 2023 World Cup, Pakistan moved away from the Arthur-Bradburn setup and brought Mohammad Hafeez into a team-director role for the Test tour of Australia and the subsequent period. The PCB's appointment of Hafeez was part of another broader restructuring, with Pakistan repeatedly changing not only coaches but also the titles and responsibilities attached to senior management positions.Then came perhaps the most ambitious coaching experiment of the period.In April 2024, Pakistan appointed Jason Gillespie as red-ball head coach and Gary Kirsten as white-ball head coach, both on two-year contracts. Azhar Mahmood was named assistant coach across all formats.The split was designed to provide specialist leadership for the two versions of the game. Kirsten, who had previously coached India to the 2011 ODI World Cup, was expected to oversee Pakistan's white-ball programme, while Gillespie was tasked with rebuilding the Test side.The arrangement, however, lasted only months. Kirsten resigned in October 2024, and the PCB handed Gillespie responsibility for the white-ball tour of Australia on an interim basis.In November, Aqib Javed was appointed interim white-ball head coach until the 2025 Champions Trophy. Gillespie's own tenure then came to an end in December 2024, after which Aqib was also given interim responsibility for the red-ball side.In effect, Pakistan had gone from a two-coach specialist model to another interim arrangement within the same calendar year.Aqib's interim white-ball tenure continued into 2025 before the PCB appointed Mike Hesson as the permanent white-ball head coach in May. Hesson took over from Aqib and began his tenure on May 26, 2025. The PCB highlighted his previous international experience with New Zealand and Kenya, as well as his work in franchise cricket.In June 2025, Azhar Mahmood was appointed acting red-ball head coach, taking over a role that had become vacant following the earlier coaching changes.Azhar subsequently continued to oversee the Test side through 2025, including the home series against South Africa. The PCB identified him as red-ball head coach for that series. The split between Hesson's white-ball role and Azhar's red-ball responsibilities appeared to offer Pakistan a chance to finally establish some continuity.But once again, the Test setup was changed.Former Pakistan captain Sarfaraz Ahmed was appointed red-ball head coach ahead of the 2026 Bangladesh Test series. The appointment was notable because Sarfaraz moved directly from a playing career into a coaching role within the national setup. He had previously worked with the Pakistan Shaheens and U19 pathway, giving him familiarity with several players coming through the system.However, his tenure lasted only a few months.Pakistan's disastrous start to the 2026 England Test series brought another dramatic intervention. After defeats in Leeds and at Lord's, the PCB removed Sarfaraz and bowling coach Umar Gul, while also sending seven players home. Hesson, who had originally been appointed as Pakistan's white-ball head coach, was brought in to take charge of the Test side as well.
Article Summary: Pakistan cricket has developed a familiar pattern over the past five years. A disappointing series or tournament is followed by a management reshuffle. Another coaching regime begins before the previous one has had enough time to establish itself. Since Misbah-ul-Haq stepped down in September 2021, the national team has gone through a succession of permanent, interim and split- format coaching arrangements.

Article Title: Towhid Hridoy creates history with 350, breaks Tamim Iqbal’s long-standing first-class record
Article Text:
Towhid Hridoy makes Bangladesh history (Image: Cricbuzz)

Hridoy breaks Tamim's record

Tamim congratulates Hridoy after record falls

Bangladesh A captain Towhid Hridoy etched his name into the country's first-class record books after becoming the first Bangladeshi batter to score 350 runs in an innings. The landmark knock came at the NWC Oval in Potchefstroom on Wednesday, more than six years after Hridoy helped Bangladesh win the Under-19 World Cup at the same venue in 2020.Resuming the fourth day on 204, Hridoy carried his bat through the remainder of Bangladesh A's innings and finished unbeaten on 350 off 481 deliveries, hitting 27 fours and 10 sixes.His innings helped Bangladesh A declare at 676 for eight, giving them a 164-run advantage after South Africa A had posted 512 in their first innings. South Africa A reached 18 without loss before the teams settled for a draw.Hridoy's marathon innings made him only the third Bangladeshi batter to reach a first-class triple century. More significantly, he went past Tamim Iqbal 's unbeaten 334 and Raqibul Hasan's unbeaten 313 to claim the highest first-class score by a Bangladeshi batter.He also became the first Bangladeshi to register a first-class 300-plus score outside the country.The 350 was equally significant from a South African perspective. Hridoy now owns the highest first-class score by an overseas batter in South Africa. Only one other batter has crossed the 350-run mark in a first-class innings in the country, Stephen Cook, who scored 390.Reflecting on the innings, Hridoy said the performance had given him considerable confidence and made him believe he could produce a similar effort at international level.“To be honest, this innings gave me a lot of confidence. After picking the Man of the Match trophy I was feeling that someday I will play an innings like this in the national team,” Hridoy said after the match.Tamim Iqbal, whose 334 had stood as Bangladesh's highest first-class score, was quick to congratulate Hridoy after his record was surpassed. Tamim said scoring 350 runs in any first-class setting was an exceptional achievement, but doing so in South Africa made the feat even more remarkable.He also welcomed the fact that his record had been broken, describing Hridoy's achievement as a sign of the progress being made by Bangladeshi cricket.South Africa A nevertheless took the four-day series 1-0. The hosts had dominated the opening match in Pretoria, winning by an innings and 413 runs, before Hridoy's record-setting performance helped Bangladesh avoid defeat in the second game.The two sides will now switch to the 50-over format, with a three-match one-day series beginning in Bloemfontein on September 6.
Article Summary: Bangladesh A captain Towhid Hridoy becomes first Bangladeshi to score 350 runs in an innings. The landmark knock came at the NWC Oval in Potchefstroom on Wednesday. He went past Tamim Iqbal's unbeaten 334 and Raqibul Hasan's unbeaten 313 to claim the highest first-class score.

Article Title: Rohit Sharma’s future, ODI roadmap to 2027 World Cup and recent setbacks on agenda at BCCI meeting

The future of Rohit Sharma and the shape of India’s ODI team for the next World Cup cycle are set to dominate discussions when the BCCI’s top brass meets in Mumbai on Thursday for a wide-ranging performance review.While recent defeats in Ireland, England and Sri Lanka will be assessed, board officials are understood to be more concerned about the lack of a clearly defined ODI roadmap at a time when preparations for the 2027 World Cup should be taking shape.BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia, president Mithun Manhas, head coach Gautam Gambhir , chief selector Ajit Agarkar and Centre of Excellence chief VVS Laxman will attend the meeting, with ODI and Test captain Shubman Gill and T20I skipper Shreyas Iyer also expected to be present.At the centre of the discussions lies the most sensitive issue facing Indian cricket: Rohit’s future. Though there is immense respect for the veteran opener’s stature and achievements, selectors and members of the team management are increasingly aware of the need to prepare for a post-Rohit era.According to sources, one option under consideration is to evaluate Rohit’s role on a series-by-series basis rather than committing to a long-term plan through the entire World Cup cycle.“It’s very tough on a young captain like Shubman Gill when there is no clear direction. The dressing-room environment in the ODI team hasn’t been the best, especially when it comes to dealing with stalwarts,” a BCCI source said.The uncertainty around Rohit reflects a broader concern. Of India’s three national teams, the ODI side is regarded as the least settled. Injuries and workload management have prevented selectors from identifying a stable core, leaving several key positions unresolved.The fast-bowling allrounder’s role remains a particular headache. Hardik Pandya continues on a managed workload programme after recurring fitness issues, while Nitish Kumar Reddy is yet to receive full clearance following rehabilitation.“Hardik, at the moment, has been cleared to bowl six overs in a day. Reddy is still to clear his fitness tests. The ODI team doesn’t have even half of the core ODI team ready. It has to be a joint effort between the CoE and the team management to zero in on players and formulate a roadmap to get them all on the park as soon as possible,” the source said.The review was initially planned after the Ireland and England tours but was postponed because of the subsequent Sri Lanka assignment. It will now cover India’s performances across multiple tours, including Zimbabwe and Sri Lanka.India’s 2-0 T20I series defeat in Ireland and the 4-0 drubbing in England raised alarm bells, with the 125-run loss at Nottingham viewed internally as one of the team’s poorest performances in recent years. Gill’s ODI side also lost the England series 2-1.However, officials insist the exercise will focus on solutions rather than assigning blame, with particular emphasis on recurring issues in preparation, selection and execution.Fitness management is expected to be another major talking point. Jasprit Bumrah missed the Sri Lanka tour after aggravating a knee problem, while Washington Sundar, Nitish Kumar Reddy and Harshit Rana remain in line for fitness assessments at the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru on Sept 9.With a two-Test tour of New Zealand scheduled for Nov and a packed calendar ahead, the board wants tighter coordination between the medical staff, strength-and-conditioning team and national selectors to ensure greater player availability.The meeting could also have significant administrative consequences. Laxman is being considered for an expanded role, with discussions continuing over a possible Director of Cricket position overseeing coaching, selection and player-development pathways. Agarkar’s tenure as chief selector, which ends later this month, will also come under review, with a one-year extension among the options being discussed.Meanwhile, BCCI is also examining the possibility of reviving the traditional Board President’s XI match before home series, following a recommendation from Manhas. The fixture, which historically featured leading domestic performers and Test hopefuls against visiting teams, has often served as a stepping stone for future India players while providing valuable match preparation to touring sides.
Article Summary: BCCI's top brass meet in Mumbai on Thursday for a wide-ranging performance review. The future of Rohit Sharma and the shape of India’s ODI team for the next World Cup cycle are set to dominate discussions. Injuries and workload management have prevented selectors from identifying a stable core, leaving key positions unresolved.

India will host the inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy in 2027, with the six-team tournament relocated from its originally designated host Sri Lanka. The tournament is scheduled to take place from February 14 to 28, 2027, marking a significant addition to India’s calendar of major women’s cricket events.The competition will feature six teams and will be played in the T20I format, with a total of 16 matches. India, Australia, England, New Zealand, South Africa and Sri Lanka have qualified for the tournament based on the ICC Women’s T20I Team Rankings.The tournament will be played across two venues, the Cricket Club of India (CCI) in Mumbai and the Vadodara International Cricket Stadium. All six teams will compete in a round-robin league stage, with the top two sides advancing to the final.Sri Lanka had originally been awarded hosting rights for the tournament. However, the ICC Board subsequently approved the move to India following a host evaluation process. Sri Lanka Cricket remains under a government-appointed committee, which the ICC considers a violation of its regulations concerning government or political interference in the administration of cricket.India emerged as the successful bidder after competing proposals from Bangladesh and South Africa were considered.“The ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027 marks an exciting new chapter for women’s cricket,” ICC Chairman Jay Shah said.“As the inaugural edition of the tournament, it will bring together the best teams in the world in an intense, high-quality competition, while creating even greater incentive for teams to continue rising through the rankings and competing for a place on the global stage,” he added.Jay Shah also highlighted the ICC’s plans to create a stronger rhythm for women’s international cricket through a regular calendar of major events.“With a marquee ICC women’s event now taking place every year, we have a significant opportunity to build greater momentum, provide more consistency and create a stronger rhythm for the women’s game, its players and its fans around the world,” he said.
